messages.author: 1641d619313d04ab
messages.subject: PML for sigma
parts:
Dear All,

I was specially interested in apply PML for variance components bounded zero, and following some threads related to that, such as:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/Xm3Pp_dIq8A

Regarding Bob's comment on that: "You can similarly penalize sigma, though that's less common in my limited experience with penalized MLE", I tried to catch the ideas in Chung et al., 2013 and also in the reference manual...

Thus, to whom it may concern, I am sharing the modified 8 schools example where applies PML for "sigma_theta". The code is working pretty well and the results agrees with what is shown in the paper.

Anyway, any comment as well as suggestions to improve shall be extremely useful :)

P.S.: I keep the names as close as possible to the original example that doesn't apply this kind of parametrization.

Kind Regards,
FH

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PML for sigma
parts:
Thanks --- you're absolutely right that you need boundary-avoiding
priors in the straight-up MLE case for hierarchical models. The
alternative, used by lme4 and other packages, is to do max marginal
likelihood. But we don't support that in Stan yet.

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PML for sigma
parts:
Hi Fernando,

I might be missing something (I often am) but I'm curious why you're calling sampling from R instead of optimizing if you're trying to do penalized MLE?

Also, to me it looks like

sigma_theta ~ gamma(...)

combined with increment_log_prob( -gamma_log(sigma_theta,...)) just works out to zero and has no effect on the log posterior. Am I missing the point of what you're trying to do?
